summaries.676: ijurica's PR for #314 clarified the SkuId, SkuPriceId and SkuPriceDetails columns. ijurica asked whether the presence conditions could be merged and when SkuId may equal SkuPriceId, and recorded TF-2 assumptions that SkuPriceId should exclude variable pricing properties and have one parent SkuId. cnharris10 requested changes, asking whether the edits let providers do as they pleased (flanakin said the intent was unchanged) and objecting to the single-parent rule with an RDS size-flexibility example. UdamDewaraja and ljadvey opposed requiring one SkuId across single and multi-AZ offerings; mike-finopsorg and rileyjenk agreed those lines went too far, and flanakin deferred several to a future release. UdamDewaraja questioned typing SkuPriceDetails as a String, and kk09v moved its requirements into #683. Members approved it on April 3, 2025, and it merged in April 2025.
summaries.683: Pull request #683, by kk09v, defined preferred keys for the SKU Price Details column (#619), narrowed to that column at shawnalpay's request. kk09v added an F_ prefix for FOCUS-defined keys and tightened them to MUST, but flanakin strongly objected that it made FOCUS feel second-class and withheld approval; shawnalpay agreed and suggested a reserved list instead. After a working group vote, provider-defined keys took an x_ prefix instead. aws-letianfeng requested changes over what InputOutput covered and how burstable 'up to' values work, leading to separate network and disk properties and a baseline-value rule. Other threads debated naming such as CoreCount and Iops, null versus empty objects, and reverting the data type to JSON. Members approved it on 3 April 2025 and it merged.
summaries.684: rileyjenk proposed guidelines for how the specification handles additions, deprecations, renames and removals, with a structured changelog and metadata properties for deprecated and previous column names. shawnalpay briefly returned it to draft in March 2025 until a TODO section was written. flanakin suggested grouping changelog entries by area and listing distinct process steps, which rileyjenk took up, but held back approval wanting a broader Status property instead of the Deprecated flag; rileyjenk argued that would turn metadata into a transactional record. rileyjenk also rejected flanakin's view that change details were too much for the changelog. mohitamzn asked about version types and support for older versions, which rileyjenk left to providers, and aws-letianfeng noted one column could replace several. Members approved it on April 3 and it merged in April 2025.
summaries.686: thecloudman opened this pull request for #615 to define an InvoiceId column and supporting content. After talking with rileyjenk, thecloudman added notes proposing a separate invoice ID table mapping invoices to rows, so providers would not need to update every row when an invoice is issued. cnharris10 asked whether the wording made the column conditional; mike-finopsorg read it as present, and null when no invoice applies. udam-f2 worried that providers such as GCP cannot restate exported data and found the uniqueness wording too strong. ijurica proposed many normative rewrites, and ljadvey and UdamDewaraja debated saying issued invoices. thecloudman dropped a rule tying each invoice to one billing account and added an editor's note on unresolved credit handling. Members approved it on February 27, 2025, and it was merged.
summaries.688: rileyjenk opened an initial appendix section of SaaS vendor examples. After UdamDewaraja wired the section into the build and exposed many content problems, UdamDewaraja proposed moving cleaned-up content to a new pull request, and task force 3 agreed to port it to #830, leaving the rest to action item #847. Maintainers agreed to close this one without merging in July 2025, and rileyjenk described it as leftovers.
summaries.689: cnharris10 fixed two bugs: period column names wrongly ending in Date, and an on-demand charge example that should have positive BilledCost and EffectiveCost. ijurica pointed out a sentence that contradicted itself for lack of a "not", plus grammatical slips in the commitment discount text. shawnalpay approved, Members approved it on 30 January, and it merged in January 2025.
summaries.691: beau-nelford-anglepoint's PR implemented #540, putting all user-defined tags in the Tags column and setting rules for providers with multiple tag schemes, following an earlier community survey. cnharris10 answered aws-letianfeng's question about tag keys containing "/" by saying providers must reserve any prefix they define, as AWS does with "aws:". ijurica suggested handling provider tag prefixes in metadata as part of #540. flanakin asked whether labels and categories clearly count as tags, wanted a MUST NOT with an exception split in two, and proposed requiring prefixes to be published in metadata; cnharris10 defended the valueless-tag exception and kept publication open-ended. kk09v confirmed exactly one user-defined scheme stays unprefixed. UdamDewaraja and shawnalpay fixed casing and punctuation. Members approved it on February 27, 2025, and it was merged.
summaries.699: cnharris10 and qquigley proposed CommitmentDiscountUnitPrice and CommitmentDiscountCost columns to break down pre- and post-negotiated discounted costs for forecasting. aws-letianfeng suggested a gross effective cost style column instead, and udam-f2 called it a niche case that would burden providers without commitments, suggesting a commitment properties column or SkuPriceDetails key. It was closed without merging in July 2025 after shawnalpay asked whether to close or repurpose it for #961, citing merge conflicts.
summaries.711: shawnalpay opened this action item in February 2025 to track continued collaboration on #676. flanakin and kk09v committed to a draft by March 12 for Task Force 2 review ahead of the March 13 PR freeze. It was closed in March 2025 once #676 came out of draft. The thread is mostly housekeeping.
summaries.716: A routine action item: shawnalpay opened it to gather reviews and approvals of #691, including whether an appendix was needed. shawnalpay chased aws-letianfeng, through jasonwucp, and flanakin, who completed a review. The issue was closed after #691 was approved at the Members meeting in February 2025.
summaries.723: shawnalpay opened this action item, with no description, for license or seat-based examples, and asked rileyjenk to coordinate with beau-nelford-anglepoint. When shawnalpay asked whether it was completed or postponed, UdamDewaraja replied that the work was done in #830, and the item was closed as completed in March 2025.
summaries.726: shawnalpay opened this action item for an example of early termination of a contract with a prorated refund, with no description. shawnalpay noted it depended on #675, then told rileyjenk to proceed without it since #675 would likely miss 1.2. rileyjenk said the item was postponed, and it remains open.
summaries.727: shawnalpay opened this action item, with no description, for an example of cancelling and replacing a contract, with a credit back and a new charge under the replacement contract. It depended on #675, but shawnalpay told rileyjenk to proceed without it because #675 would not be ready for 1.2. In March 2025 rileyjenk reported it as postponed, and the issue remained open.
summaries.736: shawnalpay opened this action item to draft guidance on the preferred mechanism for handling refunds, later moving it from the correction handling appendix to the attributes section. shawnalpay asked ahullah for updates, and with draft #675 stalled at the March 2025 pull request freeze, the work was postponed to 1.3. It was closed as not planned in July 2025 because #675 would not proceed as authored.
summaries.738: shawnalpay opened this action item to check that every cost column allowed rate exceptions for corrections, and it was postponed to 1.3 in March 2025. In July 2025 ijurica found that ListCost, ContractedCost and their related unit price and quantity columns already allowed discrepancies for corrections, but BilledCost and EffectiveCost did not. ijurica noted this for the correction handling use-case review and closed it as completed in July 2025.
summaries.740: This mostly housekeeping action item tracked drafting a PR for work item #647. JGrubb opened #747, which was blocked on #752 and later #817, then revised after TF1 discussion and syncing with flanakin. shawnalpay wanted JGrubb's high-level agreement before closing. It was closed as completed in April 2025, the draft being done though the PR itself was postponed.
summaries.747: JGrubb proposed a column, first AmortizationCategory and later AmortizationClass, marking amortized purchases and the rows they were spread across so savings calculations from ListCost and ContractedCost would not double count. shawnalpay floated widening it to commitment eligibility (#406), udam-f2 and GrinsteadJ raised negotiated burndowns and SaaS prepaid credits, GrinsteadJ suggesting Payment Category, and ijurica preferred reusing PricingCategory. A naming poll (#817) favored AmortizationClass, and flanakin held that other double-counting scenarios needed separate columns. aws-letianfeng requested wording changes for upfront-paid capacity blocks, and rileyjenk and UdamDewaraja requested changes, calling the name misleading and the scope too narrow for SaaS. After objections at the March 2025 Members meeting, maintainers pushed it to 1.3, and it was closed without merging in July 2025 to revisit in a future release.
summaries.780: rileyjenk proposed BilledCost changes (#616) to prevent double counting between vendor and marketplace FOCUS records, tying BilledCost sums to invoices from the invoice issuer. Reviewers debated the wording: cnharris10 suggested it SHOULD match and MUST NOT exceed payable invoices, while flanakin urged being ambitious and letting data generators document coverage gaps. thecloudman proposed saying "finalized" invoices rather than listing estimate invoices, and ijurica asked whether such charges should be zero and whether naming the invoice issuer added anything. UdamDewaraja found combining billing period, billing account and InvoiceId problematic. After TF-2 on March 27, ijurica suggested matching the sum for a given InvoiceId to that invoice's payable amount. shawnalpay asked rileyjenk to resolve open threads before the members vote. Members approved it on April 3, 2025, and it merged that month.
summaries.787: For #557 and FOCUS 1.2, ijurica set out guidelines for writing column normative requirements and rewrote a first set of columns to match, with the rest in #798; reviewers were asked to flag unintended changes. flanakin questioned dropping "globally" from globally unique identifiers, doubted providers could guarantee unique billing account names, a point thecloudman echoed, and found "exclusive ending bound" unclear. shawnalpay resisted changing requirement strength within a consistency review, keeping ChargeDescription length a SHOULD. qquigley asked why both SHOULD and RECOMMENDED appeared; ijurica said RECOMMENDED marked presence rules tied to feature levels. smokemonster99 queried renamed column references, which ijurica said followed the editorial guidelines. Unresolved points went to a list of discussion topics. Members approved it in March 2025 and it was merged.
summaries.798: This was the second part of ijurica's rewrite of column normative requirements under the #557 guidelines, with #787 covering the other columns. ijurica flagged deliberate changes already agreed in TF-1: fixing CommitmentDiscountQuantity's positive-only value range as a bug, rewording EffectiveCost rules for unused commitments, and aligning nullability for quantity and unit pairs. flanakin proposed EffectiveCost wording linking purchase and usage costs, and answered thecloudman's doubt about tax examples. SkuPriceDetails was declared a String with key-value format, and another SkuPriceDetails change was reverted after UdamDewaraja raised a concern, with follow-up logged as #855. cnharris10 and ijurica reworked how the Tags requirements were grouped, and smokemonster99 caught typos. Members approved it in April 2025 and it was merged.
summaries.799: shawnalpay proposed two columns for work item #616: PricingCurrency, covering virtual currencies such as tokens or credits as well as government-issued ones, and PricingCurrencyToBillingCurrency, a conversion factor. The PR also widened CurrencyCodeFormat into CurrencyFormat and denominated list and contracted unit prices in the pricing currency. After TF3 discussion it dropped earlier Pricing Denomination names. flanakin called fiat jargon, wanted calculations kept in billing currency, suggested a shorter name such as BillingExchangeRate and asked about the exchange-rate date; shawnalpay defended self-documenting names and questioned needing the date. ijurica raised Microsoft mappings and presence options and noted #318 had proposed almost the same thing. amitkinha approved. shawnalpay closed it in March 2025, replaced by #848, which renamed the rate column Pricing To Billing Exchange Rate and used national instead of fiat.
summaries.807: shawnalpay opened this action item to resolve the editor's note in the Invoice ID column. The fix in #828 waited on whether #675 would make version 1.2; when shawnalpay judged that unlikely, thecloudman was told to proceed without it. The group suggested removing the editor's note and adding a note to the supporting document, and shawnalpay closed the item in March 2025 after confirming with thecloudman.
summaries.810: shawnalpay opened this action item in February 2025 to prevent double counting in Effective Cost, alongside the Billed Cost work. rileyjenk narrowed it so the Effective Cost question would not hold up the Billed Cost changes. shawnalpay suggested it was complete once #780 left draft, but after speaking with rileyjenk recorded in March 2025 that the work was postponed to 1.3.
summaries.817: shawnalpay opened this action item to settle a column name through a spreadsheet or vote, including use cases, and in March 2025 pressed flanakin on whether a poll existed, warning that the related pull request might miss its deadline. A naming spreadsheet for the double-counting column was then shared. It was closed as completed in March 2025 with no further discussion.
summaries.828: thecloudman proposed credit-handling requirements for the InvoiceId column (#615). shawnalpay suggested condensing them and asked ahullah and ijurica to review, mike-finopsorg proposed rules for credits in the current billing period, and flanakin made editorial points. After TF-2 discussion, thecloudman moved the credit handling into supporting content and set the feature level to Recommended at ijurica's suggestion. Members approved it in March 2025 and it merged.
summaries.834: rileyjenk proposed refactoring the definitions of provider, publisher, invoice issuer and data generator, citing inconsistent use of provider and a Host Provider name implying hierarchy. shawnalpay noted host relationships could be many-to-many, ijurica suggested reviewing display names, and GrinsteadJ argued for multiple data generators and an optional HostProvider. Maintainers limited it to definition clarifications. It closed in March 2025, split into #839 and #843, leftovers going to a work item.
summaries.839: rileyjenk proposed a Host Provider column for #616. flanakin requested changes, calling it a half-finished rename of Publisher and Provider that reused "provider" confusingly, while shawnalpay warned that delay would push providers into custom columns. In March 2025 it was postponed to 1.3 because it needed a wider refactor of Provider, Publisher and Invoice Issuer, and in June 2025 it was closed without merging in favor of rileyjenk's #1139.
summaries.843: rileyjenk split out a rename of the metadata property Provider Version to Data Generator Version from a larger pull request. mike-finopsorg asked whether it should also update the changelog; shawnalpay treated the changelog as a consistency review task. flanakin suggested the newer bulleted requirement style, and shawnalpay explained metadata had not been put in that scope. Members approved it on April 3 and it merged in April 2025.
summaries.844: rileyjenk added to the spec a clarification on how FOCUS uses Semantic Versioning, agreed at an August 2024 maintainers meeting but never written in (#643). shawnalpay suggested README wording. Members approved it on March 27, 2025, and it was merged that month.
summaries.848: shawnalpay proposed four columns for prices set in a virtual or different currency (PricingCurrency, PricingCurrencyEffectiveCost, PricingCurrencyListUnitPrice and PricingCurrencyContractedUnitPrice), replacing #799 because some members rejected redefining existing unit price columns; existing columns stayed unchanged. cnharris10 supported the aim but feared moving too fast without modelled data, so mike-finopsorg shared a sample sheet. thecloudman asked whether a priced cost column duplicated Billed Cost, and ijurica proposed simpler presence conditions. daviddinhgcp proposed separate token and local currency columns; mike-finopsorg replied that conversion works the same for national and virtual currencies and extra columns would widen the spec. On March 31, 2025 maintainers struck the exchange rate column and deferred exchange rates to a future release. Members approved the PR on April 3, 2025, and it was merged that day.
summaries.854: shawnalpay opened this March 2025 issue as a running list of 1.2 consistency review tasks, such as file naming, CSV examples, a stray table row and the changelog, each spun off into its own action item, and ijurica proposed more. At the April 7, 2025 maintainers meeting, revisiting "amortization" in EffectiveCost and settling row versus charge versus record were deferred to a future release. The thread doesn't record its closure.
summaries.857: This action item, from #830, asked for fixes to data issues in the Simple and Spend SaaS Agreement examples. ijurica compiled proposed changes and raised whether ConsumedQuantity requirements fit unused-fee rows and whether ListCost and ContractedCost should be 0 on them, preferring 0. UdamDewaraja and ijurica aligned on the sheet, and UdamDewaraja took on CSV conversion following #896. It was closed as completed in April 2025.
summaries.873: This mostly editorial PR by flanakin removed unnecessary references to "row" from column definitions. jpradocueva asked whether "charge" should be italicised or linked, which became moot when the word was dropped, and shawnalpay opposed ijurica's suggestion to describe account types as names rather than identifiers. Members approved it on 17 April 2025, and it was merged.
summaries.882: shawnalpay reorganized the appendix under action item #881, renaming entries with an Examples prefix. At UdamDewaraja's suggestion the entries were sorted alphabetically, and with rileyjenk's agreement an outdated metadata example still using Provider Version wording was removed. The change was mainly editorial; Members approved it on April 17 and it merged in April 2025.
summaries.891: thecloudman proposed relaxing the BillingCurrency rule that it match the invoice currency from MUST to SHOULD, because AWS exports bill in USD while invoices may be in other currencies. shawnalpay said the MUST dated back to release 0.5 and could not change during consistency review, suggesting a work item for 1.3. Maintainers closed it in July 2025 until a future release or an active advocate takes it up.
summaries.892: Matt-Cowsert's first PR, under #877, fixed typos and simple grammar issues across the spec for the 1.2 release. shawnalpay asked to back out an edit to a metadata example because #900 would rework that file, and Matt-Cowsert agreed; ijurica moved a separate fix, a missing "not", to another item. shawnalpay approved, Members approved it on April 17, 2025, and it was merged.
summaries.896: shawnalpay converted the commitment discount and commitment discount flexibility appendix examples from embedded JSON to linked CSV files, under action item #863, with SaaS examples handled in #908 and metadata kept in JSON. Relative links to the CSV files worked on GitHub but not in the HTML and PDF build, which mike-finopsorg fixed in #904. Members approved it on April 17 and it merged in April 2025.
summaries.899: ijurica proposed updating ConsumedQuantity requirements so unused portions of commitments, such as monthly unused fees, were handled without relying on CommitmentDiscountStatus, plus guidance for missing data in SaaS scenarios. UdamDewaraja said it was too late in the cycle and that commitment status needed rethinking, and shawnalpay agreed to defer it. It was closed without merging in July 2025 after ijurica judged the problem fell within #976 on negotiated commitments.
summaries.905: ijurica proposed fixing post-merge inconsistencies in the SKU and SKU Price columns for AI #902, plus best-effort editorial changes. shawnalpay requested changes, agreeing to remove a duplicated SkuPriceDetails requirement but saying the consistency review was not the time to reword normative requirements or rewrite the description. Members approved the PR on April 17, 2025, and it was merged that day.
summaries.908: UdamDewaraja converted the SaaS appendix examples to CSV under action item #863. shawnalpay approved but worried the columns were neither fully alphabetical nor ordered by importance; ljadvey favoured alphabetical order for simplicity, and UdamDewaraja preferred grouping related columns but noted earlier votes for alphabetical. UdamDewaraja then found the columns already sorted, shawnalpay withdrew the concern, and it merged in April 2025 after Members approved it.
summaries.910: ijurica proposed clarifying that FOCUS-defined SkuPriceDetails properties take precedence over equivalent provider-defined ones. shawnalpay questioned treating this as a fix during consistency review, and kk09v read the rule as intentionally requiring both; it was postponed to 1.3 in April 2025. In July ijurica adopted kk09v's rewording and reverted a SHOULD-to-MUST change after kk09v objected. Members approved it on September 4, 2025.
summaries.914: ijurica's pull request (#913) made best-effort editorial adjustments, mainly to column specs, adding links to glossary terms and columns and aligning formatting with the editorial guidelines. shawnalpay approved it with one small suggestion on Charge Category. Members approved it on April 17, 2025, and it merged.
summaries.956: Matt-Cowsert opened this in May 2025 asking FOCUS to carry provider-calculated cost splits below the machine level, such as containers, pods and tasks, citing AWS, GCP, OCI and Azure features; many organisations registered support. shawnalpay argued the data adds rows and columns, so practitioners must be able to opt in (#1091, #1093). UdamDewaraja objected to calling it shared cost allocation, and TF-2 renamed it in July 2025. TF-2 compared split lines, double-entry rows and a secondary dataset; a poll (#1322) favoured split lines, while rileyjenk and jasonwucp worried about breaking existing reports. The group agreed allocations must reconcile to the original charge, be flagged and use a JSON details column (#1383). #1394, stewarded by kk09v and qquigley, was approved and merged in September 2025, closing the request as complete.
summaries.958: Matt-Cowsert asked for an indicator showing which non-negotiated discount programs, such as commitment discounts or SaaS public pricing tiers, a charge was eligible for, to support coverage and savings-rate analysis. qquigley supported a simple boolean but warned that hypothetical cost columns could taint reporting; shawnalpay suggested a JSON column of eligibility flags. Scoped for 1.3, it was repeatedly bumped and then descoped in August 2025. From November 2025 SanjnaSrivatsaVMware sponsored and drafted it in Task Force 3, where the group chose JSON over a boolean, broadened scope beyond commitment discounts after cnharris10 raised hybrid SaaS cases, added capacity reservations, and made negotiated programs a MAY. The name became Commitment Program Eligibility Details, and shawnalpay closed the issue in April 2026 after #1882 and #2025 merged.
summaries.962: Matt-Cowsert asked in May 2025 for an overarching correction-handling attribute, because correction rules were scattered across individual columns and practitioners needed to reconcile corrections with invoices. Most comments were task force updates from shawnalpay. ijurica split the work into several PRs, including #1241, #1242 and #1245 tightening existing column requirements, #1368 for the attribute and #1434 for examples. In October 2025 the maintainers deferred #1368, refactored as #1501, until an Invoice dataset (#1500) could ground rules on when data generators may revise invoiced data. By January 2026 #1501 covered both delivery handling and correction handling, and in March ijurica and rileyjenk agreed to split it further. Members merged #1434 and #1501, and shawnalpay closed the request as complete in April 2026.
summaries.966: Matt-Cowsert asked for a way for data generators to state how recent and complete a FOCUS dataset is. TF-2 found the original scope hard for providers, so rileyjenk narrowed it to optional metadata with generators setting their own completeness thresholds; davidearney asked how later data changes would be handled. The work landed in #1374 and #1464, tying recency to charge period, and the issue closed as completed in October 2025.
summaries.975: Matt-Cowsert opened this feature request for a normalized recommendations dataset, because practitioners receive optimization recommendations such as rightsizing and commitment purchases from many providers in different formats; eleven organizations backed it. In 2026 the work moved to task force 2 through #2444, and the thread recorded decisions there: evaluation period start and end columns with duration deferred, past-participle date column names, and RecommendationProviderName in place of DataGeneratorName. flanakin and rileyjenk disagreed over resource configuration columns, and the scope was trimmed before initial Member review in September 2026. In October 2026 maintainers moved the dataset and its supported feature, #2583, to the 1.6 cycle for lack of consensus on its shape and names. The request remained open.
summaries.976: Matt-Cowsert asked FOCUS to represent contract-negotiated commitments, such as burn-down and build-up agreements, so practitioners could track progress against them; NASA, Autodesk, Atlassian, Google and others added support. Task Force 1 began in June 2025 with goals of giving each negotiated commitment an ID, linking usage to it and describing its terms. ijurica noted a single contract ID could not show drawdown against individual line items, and shawnalpay floated a mandatory Contract ID with an optional Commitment ID. shawnalpay renamed the request and opened #1327, then #1350. In August 2025 most participants favored always requiring the proposed JSON datapoints for usability, while cnharris10 and partly richkreitz prioritized dataset size. #1350 merged in September 2025, closing the request, with follow-on work in #1459.
summaries.982: Matt-Cowsert opened this in May 2025 because ambiguous EffectiveCost and BilledCost definitions led data generators to implement them inconsistently, including a rule zeroing BilledCost for all marketplace purchases. Through 2025 Task Force 3 split over partial-upfront commitments: rileyjenk wanted billed cost distributed to usage records, while ijurica wanted it kept on purchase records. In September 2025 the work was cut from 1.3. For 1.4 the group reframed the problem as accuracy rather than double counting, adopted three milestones and, as shawnalpay urged, avoided the term amortization. Definitions were refined in #1678, and #1966 rewrote the normative requirements around covered and covering charges and the invoice issuer. After #1966 and #2022 were approved and merged, shawnalpay closed it as complete in April 2026.
summaries.1024: Matt-Cowsert asked for clearer SkuPriceDetails rules, because the wording implied both a FOCUS-defined property and its provider-defined equivalent must appear, rather than preferring the FOCUS-defined one. flanakin supported it but said a PR would be better than task force time, and ijurica noted FOCUS-defined properties were new in 1.2. shawnalpay closed it as complete in September 2025 after #910 merged.
summaries.1026: Matt-Cowsert proposed replacing RECOMMENDED with SHOULD throughout the spec, since RFC 2119 treats the two as equivalent and mixing them could confuse implementers. Matt-Cowsert asked whether practitioners had reported problems; jpradocueva knew of none, and qquigley supported it while expecting it to be a low priority. In February 2026 shawnalpay said #1647 had already done the work and closed the request.
summaries.1055: Matt-Cowsert asked to clarify the ambiguous Provider, Publisher and Invoice Issuer columns, deferred from 1.2. jasonwucp urged setting breaking-change criteria first, and ijurica flagged inconsistent display names. Task Force 3 agreed in September 2025 to deprecate Provider and Publisher in favor of service provider and host provider columns, and shortened the deprecation window to one release. shawnalpay closed it in October 2025 after #1139, #1505 and #1524 were approved.
summaries.1056: Matt-Cowsert requested a clearer JSON data type and a strategy for structured JSON columns, because the key-value format caused naming collisions, could not hold complex structures, and left unclear whether JSON or serialized strings were meant. shawnalpay first asked for examples, then pulled the work into 1.3 because the proposals for #962 and #956 used arrays of JSON objects. It was closed as completed in September 2025 after #1383 merged.
summaries.1057: Matt-Cowsert requested a separate dataset of a provider's SKUs and prices for lookups, joins and pre-purchase estimation. shawnalpay asked for scope and use cases and distinguished a SKU dataset from a SKU Price dataset. From May 2026 shawnalpay drafted a model and #2424, which Matt-Cowsert stewarded during shawnalpay's leave. Task Force 1 worked through tier boundaries, PricingCategory, dropping ChargeFrequency, snapshot versus history, and the dataset's condition, keeping IncludesUnitPricing in September 2026. The longest dispute was two price columns on one row versus one row per price under a single UnitPrice; shawnalpay argued for rows to avoid fabricated effective dates, while flanakin's queryability concern stayed open. Members approved releasing the dataset as a preview on October 22, 2026, and GitHub shows the issue closed as completed on 31 October 2026.
summaries.1059: ijurica opened this in May 2025 because FOCUS had no formal guidelines for writing attribute specifications, risking inconsistent or unclear requirements; the plan was to write guidelines and apply them to existing attributes without material changes. shawnalpay pointed to precedent PRs #787 and #798 and later urged priority, since compound requirements such as those in Discount Handling were hard to turn into conformance rules. The item moved between task forces and went undiscussed for months until February 2026, when ijurica presented #1967 (guidelines) and #1981 (refactoring), rephrasing requirements as verifiable states for the FOCUS Validator. A few deliberate material changes were accepted and others deferred. For binding requirements to custom columns, mike-finopsorg proposed a hybrid approach. shawnalpay closed it as complete in April 2026 after #1967, #1981 and #2166 merged.
summaries.1070: Issue #1070, opened by Matt-Cowsert in May 2025, argued that FOCUS's use of 'commitment discount' excluded negotiated commitments and assumed a burn-down model, which caused problems for SaaS. shawnalpay asked how it overlapped with #976, and ijurica gathered the existing glossary definitions. In September 2025 it was renamed and moved from 1.3 to 1.4 as tied to Contract Commitment work in #1459. It closed in March 2026, completed via #1964.
summaries.1073: Matt-Cowsert requested a way to show the cloud provider hosting a SaaS service such as Snowflake, which the Provider, Publisher and Invoice Issuer definitions did not capture. shawnalpay reframed it as a Host Provider request, questioned its use cases and made it depend on #1055. Matt-Cowsert later noted its scope was covered by #1139, and shawnalpay closed it as complete in October 2025 after the related PRs merged.
summaries.1082: Matt-Cowsert asked that the spec state every charge on an invoice must appear in FOCUS data, so BilledCost reconciles to the invoice. shawnalpay pressed for taxes and indirect charges such as training to be covered. TF-3 drafted an invoice handling attribute in #1321, debating SHOULD versus MUST, duplication and payable splits, and kept a single MUST. #1321 merged and the request closed as complete in September 2025.
summaries.1090: robmartin33 asked in May 2025 for FOCUS to be organised as related datasets, for easier use in BI tools, so finer detail could be added without bloating the main dataset. shawnalpay strongly supported it as a star schema, referencing #1006. In June 2025 the group agreed a six-week spike, ruling out a star schema for 1.3. Task Force 2 then produced design principles (#1150) and dataset definitions (#1337), rejecting fact and dimension terminology as too database-specific in favour of names like FOCUS Cost and Usage plus machine-readable IDs, and requiring datasets to be independent but joinable. Maintainers adopted dataset-level normative requirements, and #1431 tied attributes to datasets. A second dataset was left to #976 and editorial cleanup to consistency review. shawnalpay closed it as complete in October 2025.
summaries.1091: Matt-Cowsert asked in May 2025 for data generators to let practitioners choose which columns to export, and maintainers debated whether this was within FOCUS's remit. #1816 first added aggregation and time granularity; shawnalpay objected that aggregation belonged to consumers, and flanakin disagreed but accepted dropping it, which thecloudman and mike-finopsorg supported. #1816 was approved and merged, and the issue was closed in February 2026.
summaries.1094: Matt-Cowsert asked that FOCUS datasets carry custom x_ columns for any native billing data not covered by FOCUS columns, so practitioners could rely on FOCUS alone. ijurica added correlation use cases, such as carrying a provider's unique charge ID as a custom column. flanakin said only MUST would achieve the goal, though SHOULD might win provider buy-in, and in January 2026 opened #1800 with a new Scenario Completeness attribute. A provider-side request to soften MUST to SHOULD was settled by keeping MUST while letting data generators default to a subset of columns. The group made correlation a separate SHOULD and, in March 2026, simplified the core rule to include all native columns except documented, justified exclusions. #1800 merged and shawnalpay closed the issue in March 2026.
summaries.1124: Matt-Cowsert opened this request because practitioners could not tell which charges can be tagged or where a tag value came from. With kk09v and qquigley as sponsors and work starting in 1.4, TF-2 widened it from resource to charge tagging after cnharris10 noted SaaS tags without resources, and ruled out SKUs as the basis. From eleven candidate structures the group chose a key-driven TagDetails column alongside Tags, after kk09v's BigQuery tests, drafted as #1904. An AWS test showed data growing seven to eight times, tying it to column selection (#1091). In March 2026 shawnalpay opposed adding Recommended columns; maintainers found little support for #1904 as written, felt the scope had grown without re-review, and believed time had run out in the release.
summaries.1139: rileyjenk opened this pull request in June 2025 for #1055 and #1073, after feedback that the Provider and Publisher columns were confusing. It deprecated PublisherName and ProviderName and added Service Provider and Host Provider columns, the latter for vendors running on other providers' infrastructure. Because this was FOCUS's first deprecation, shawnalpay asked for a summary and a link to the deprecation guidelines. flanakin objected that renaming Provider would force customers to change their queries and suggested calling the new column Host; rileyjenk replied that Host alone was ambiguous and naming was better fixed now. Reviewers also debated whether a FinOps vendor is a data generator, with editorial follow-ups moved to #1226 and #1336. Members approved it on October 16, 2025, and it was merged that month.
summaries.1151: ijurica proposed formalising a broader meaning of correction, covering any update to a previously generated charge whatever its invoicing status, through scenarios, examples, column requirements and a new CorrectionHandling attribute that would bar replacement-style corrections after a billing period closed. The task force agreed to rename restatement to replacement. It was closed without merging in August 2025 as a demonstration pull request, superseded by #1241, #1242, #1245 and #1368.
summaries.1171: shawnalpay opened this action item for a draft pull request of example scenarios for correction handling, with candidate scenarios gathered in a shared spreadsheet. It replaced action item #756, after the group dropped #675 in favor of #1151. ijurica prepared the examples while the due date slipped several times. Once ijurica opened draft #1434, task force 1 reviewed it and the item was closed as completed in September 2025.
summaries.1173: This action item asked for PRs introducing a Correction Handling attribute and its supporting content. ijurica brought a draft, and TF1 reviewed #1368, a lift-and-shift from #1151, in August 2025. Once #1368 was authored, shawnalpay noted PRs now covered the whole feature request and closed the item as completed in August 2025. The thread is mostly housekeeping.
summaries.1239: ijurica proposed clarifying the definition and requirements of EffectiveCost under #982, and built a sample dataset of standalone and prepaid-coverage scenarios. ijurica disputed a proposal describing BilledCost as accrual-based, calling it invoice-based; UdamDewaraja suggested separating or unifying amortization and drawdown cases, and cnharris10 found the text overly complex and asked for examples. It was closed without merging in September 2025, removed from 1.3 to revisit in 1.4.
summaries.1240: Matt-Cowsert opened this action item in August 2025 to draft an invoice-handling attribute, describing how invoiced charges relate to the FOCUS dataset, and review it with members (#1321). TF-3 asked for more specificity, chose to reference charge category requirements rather than repeat them, and parked the charge versus row debate (#1027). In August 2025 shawnalpay asked to close it once the draft was ready for member review, and Matt-Cowsert agreed.
summaries.1321: Matt-Cowsert proposed an invoice handling attribute for FR #1082, requiring FOCUS datasets to cover every invoiced charge. shawnalpay asked for it to be applied to every affected column and for Invoice ID to cover all charges; flanakin objected that one billing period can have several invoices, so the original wording returned with a clarification. UdamDewaraja wanted prepaid usage statements included, warned invoices cannot be expected to use FOCUS terms, and argued the core rule was that totals per invoice ID match the invoice. flanakin asked where the line lay; ijurica floated limiting it to IT costs, and shawnalpay and ijurica proposed scoping it to invoices issued to a billing account. Task Force 3 struck duplicative requirements. Members approved it on September 25, 2025; it merged the next day.
summaries.1323: rileyjenk drafted a change to the EffectiveCost description to make clear it includes amortized upfront fees, recurring fees and non-prepaid fees, for FR #982. shawnalpay gave process feedback: the PDF build failed on smart quotes, and the PR lacked an FR prefix and a full description. rileyjenk closed it without merging in August 2025 and moved the content into #1239.
summaries.1325: This action item tracked revisions to the completeness metadata pull request: making completeness declarations a SHOULD, not a MUST, for data generators, and clarifying time sector requirements. Matt-Cowsert logged repeated TF-2 check-ins on rileyjenk's #1374; ijurica and vikramdesai01 questioned time sector semantics, and the group agreed time sectors apply only to usage, not billing periods. It closed as completed in September 2025 once TF-2 judged it ready for member review.
summaries.1334: shawnalpay's action item was to draft a PR adding contract attributes such as start date and amount, needed to complete #976 beyond the columns in #1327. It was briefly blocked on #1090 until the August 11, 2025 Maintainers call set a direction. shawnalpay drafted #1350, revised it after TF1 feedback on contractual commitments, and closed the item in September 2025 once #1350 left draft.
summaries.1336: shawnalpay opened this action item in August 2025 to review the spec's 149 uses of "provider" and replace them with terms such as service provider, host provider or data generator, following #1055 and #1139. shawnalpay urged starting early in 1.3 development; rileyjenk volunteered but preferred waiting until spec development finished. The work landed in #1567, which was approved and merged, and the item closed in November 2025.
summaries.1337: Pull request #1337, by mike-finopsorg, reorganized the repository layout to support multiple FOCUS datasets (#1090). shawnalpay requested that the existing dataset be called Cost and Usage rather than the FOCUS dataset, since any FOCUS dataset should count as one. flanakin objected that duplicating columns per dataset would not scale; shawnalpay replied that maintainers had reached consensus on it in August. Members approved it on 28 August 2025 and it merged.
summaries.1349: shawnalpay's second draft, following #1327, added ContractId and a ContractApplied JSON column to the Cost and Usage dataset to link charges to contract commitments. cnharris10 asked why a JSON object was preferred over four dedicated columns, and rileyjenk noted the key-value format could not show two commitments applying to one charge without arrays. It was closed without merging in August 2025 in favour of the more holistic #1350.
summaries.1350: For #976, shawnalpay proposed a ContractApplied JSON column linking each cost row to the contract commitments it counts toward, plus a new Contract Commitment dataset describing those commitments. kk09v argued for a true JSON object format with a defined schema, which led to #1383 and kk09v's #1462, and ijurica wanted custom properties declared in metadata. After flanakin asked how several contracts could apply to one charge, ContractId moved inside the array. cnharris10 questioned having both type and description columns, and marc-perreaut's idea for handling values redundant with other columns was weighed against added complexity. Maintainers let data generators omit inapplicable cost, quantity or unit values, and BillingCurrency replaced a separate currency column. shawnalpay offered to defer ContractCommitmentType to #1459. Members approved it in September 2025 and it was merged.
summaries.1368: ijurica proposed a Correction Handling attribute for FR #962, setting rules for how corrections appear depending on whether original records were invoiced and whether data is delivered by replacement or append-only. jasonwucp asked which corrections are handled by restating past months. rileyjenk argued for a fundamental rethink: let data generators correct data whatever the mechanism, with separate rules for billed cost in closed and open periods, usage and EffectiveCost, and non-cost fields. shawnalpay asked that a normative requirement use the attribute and that invoice rules move to an Invoice Handling attribute from #1321; flanakin doubted invoice requirements belonged in a cost dataset. SatyaVandrangi1 questioned strict immutability, since invoices can be cancelled and reissued. In October 2025 shawnalpay closed it in favour of #1501, a heavy refactor done with ijurica.
summaries.1374: rileyjenk proposed adding recency metadata under feature request #966, with properties for time sectors, completeness and last-updated dates, and examples for datasets that do and do not change over time. shawnalpay asked for a more specific name than Complete, which rileyjenk agreed to fix. Matt-Cowsert requested changes, mostly cleanup and tighter wording, preferred the terms time-series and non-time-series, and asked whether the JSON examples were meant to be prescriptive; rileyjenk replied that metadata structure had traditionally been non-prescriptive and that a should would have to become a must everywhere. Matt-Cowsert then approved, and ijurica approved while noting editorial items for the 1.3 consistency review. It moved to Member review in September 2025, was approved at the October 2 Members' meeting and merged in October 2025.
summaries.1380: shawnalpay opened this issue in August 2025 to collect work for the 1.3 consistency review, planned for October 16 to 30. Contributors logged many items, each turned into an action item or pull request: adding Requirements subheaders (#1508), restructuring supporting content (#1510), replacing "term" with "duration" (#1493), JSON string versus object typing (#1480), standardizing .mdpp files (#1512), drafting changelog entries, fixing the Commitment definition to include spend (#1514), clarifying "data artifact" and "FOCUS dataset" usage (#1515), and ijurica's EffectiveCost wording and nesting suggestions. Matt-Cowsert reported TF-3 agreed to revert display-name changes on deprecated columns; shawnalpay argued that belonged in #1139 rather than consistency review. Remaining items were assigned in October task force meetings, and the issue closed when 1.3 was released in December 2025.
summaries.1382: shawnalpay reported that the HTML and PDF builder numbered duplicate anchors for columns used in several datasets, which would break links as datasets were added, and proposed prefixing anchors with the dataset name. mike-finopsorg suggested extending the vendored Markdown-PP tool to build anchors from the full heading path, and shawnalpay widened the scope to name overlaps between attributes and supported features. It was completed through #1656 in January 2026.
summaries.1383: kk09v revived an earlier object format idea from flanakin for #1056, because several feature requests needed complex JSON objects that the key-value format could not hold. kk09v renamed it from JSON Object Format to Object Format, since the data type already says JSON, and explored how to describe object shapes, finding RFC 8927 useful but not very human-readable. In maintainer meetings, ijurica asked that custom provider object columns carry public documentation or schema metadata, which kk09v added, and the group settled a nesting limit, worded as SHOULD NOT exceed 3 levels. A straw poll was planned on keeping JTD schemas inside column definitions, which ijurica favoured. qquigley raised wording points. shawnalpay approved, and it was approved at the September 18 members' meeting and merged in September 2025.
summaries.1389: mike-finopsorg proposed moving normative requirements that apply to a whole dataset, chiefly column presence rules, into each dataset definition, rephrased so the dataset carries the requirement. shawnalpay saw it as a subset of #1090, and the work was combined with #1796. Task Force 2 confirmed the approach in January 2026. It closed via #1865 in February 2026, was reopened for #2138, and closed again in April 2026.
summaries.1394: kk09v and qquigley proposed provider-calculated split cost allocation (#956), adding AllocatedResourceId, AllocatedResourceName, AllocatedMethodId, AllocatedTags and a details column, plus an attribute, a supported feature and glossary terms. TF-2 reshaped the details column into an array of objects with a JSON schema, later named AllocatedMethodDetails, and moved the method into its own column. jpradocueva asked that requirements target dataset entities rather than providers, and rileyjenk objected to requiring providers to support a feature, so kk09v softened the wording. flanakin questioned the term "allocated method" and whether ratios were fractions or percentages, and Cosmos DB cases went to #1479. shawnalpay pressed for a change summary, a fixed PDF build and resolved conflicts. Members approved it on 25 September 2025 and it merged.
summaries.1396: Matt-Cowsert opened this action item in August 2025 to resolve review comments on #1394, about provider-calculated split cost allocation, ahead of the 1.3 release. TF-2 worked through the comments over several weeks, and qquigley asked whether a name change to allocated method details had been agreed. In September 2025 shawnalpay declared it done after members reviewed #1394 with no open threads.
summaries.1431: shawnalpay proposed this for #1090 because the spec said attributes applied to all FOCUS datasets, which would be inaccurate once more existed; it associated every current attribute with the Cost and Usage dataset. flanakin questioned a line on when datasets are required, and shawnalpay explained only Cost and Usage is always required. ijurica suggested more dataset glossary terms. Members approved it on September 11, 2025, and it was merged.
summaries.1433: kk09v proposed adding an Unallocated option to AllocatedMethodId so data could show whether a charge was allocated, allocatable but not allocated, or not allocatable. When shawnalpay pointed out a merge conflict, kk09v said it might not be needed. kk09v closed it without merging in September 2025 as no longer necessary.
summaries.1434: ijurica proposed a Correction Handling Examples appendix section (feature request #962) covering corrections to current and previous open billing periods and to closed periods, using Overwrite and Append delivery and Replacement, Delta and Ledger correction styles. Task force 1 asked for a scenario overview, then in October 2025 agreed to postpone the work, and shawnalpay closed the pull request. It resumed for 1.4, with ijurica updating the terminology in January 2026. caligo-erik flagged repeated links, and pydi-aws questioned assigning corrections to the next open billing period rather than the original, which shawnalpay agreed to revisit in task force 1. Once the examples became CSV files, shawnalpay found many errors, including swapped Delta and Ledger data, which ijurica fixed. Members approved it on April 2 and it merged in April 2026.
summaries.1446: flanakin added "Name" to the display names of InvoiceIssuerName, ProviderName and PublisherName so they matched their column IDs (#1055). shawnalpay asked for a full scrub of other references and worried about overlap with #1139, which would deprecate Publisher; ijurica asked that descriptions begin with the column name. Members approved it on October 2, 2025, and it was merged that month.
summaries.1449: Matt-Cowsert opened this action item to finish the draft pull request on EffectiveCost and BilledCost, #1239, and keep #982 in the 1.3 scope. UdamDewaraja agreed to lead the effort, and the group agreed to drop the work from 1.3 if no path forward emerged by late September. With no resolution reached, it was cut from 1.3 and closed as not planned in September 2025, to continue in 1.4.
summaries.1458: shawnalpay noted in September 2025 that spec text often assumed "a FOCUS dataset" meant the Cost and Usage dataset, citing Column Handling wording raised by ijurica, and asked for a scrub. After TF-2 discussion, Matt-Cowsert added it to the 1.3 consistency review (#1380). Matt-Cowsert closed it in October 2025 after the related pull request was approved at the members meeting.
summaries.1459: shawnalpay proposed in September 2025 extending the Contract Commitment dataset, founded in 1.3 by #1350 under #976, with columns for balances, scope rules, attestation and commitment models. It was paired with #1070 for 1.4, and Task Force 1 asked for use cases, examples and supported features. A data model drafted in January 2026 became PR #1924. shawnalpay closed it in March 2026 as completed via #1924, continuing in #1938.
summaries.1464: rileyjenk opened this pull request for FR #966 to let data generators declare dataset instances, each with an ID and a name, after finding the recency work could not cleanly handle a generator supplying several outputs of the same FOCUS dataset. ijurica and rileyjenk went back and forth on what to call the dataset reference property, and rileyjenk kept free-form instance names in the examples and noted that FOCUS version already sits in schema metadata. udam-stitcher asked for crisper definitions separating a FOCUS dataset from a dataset instance, and shawnalpay's request to move prose out of the mdpp file was deferred to consistency review. Matt-Cowsert requested editorial changes, then approved. Members approved it on 2 October and it merged in October 2025, with a terminology consistency pass added to #1380.
summaries.1488: Matt-Cowsert asked for appendix line-item examples for non-negotiated commitments (reserved instances, savings plans, CUDs) that explain why each column holds its value, so providers could implement them correctly and practitioners could validate their data. The thread logged TF-2 progress. ljadvey was assigned in January 2026, and the group chose provider-specific data, kept charge subcategory out of scope, and agreed to replace rather than supplement the existing appendix examples, with the work done in #1877. There, ijurica flagged duplicate rows and the undefined term "effective unit price", and thecloudman flagged a misleading claim that BilledCost equals ListCost. In March the group removed non-EC2 rows and savings calculations and pushed commitment eligibility to a later feature request. shawnalpay closed it as completed in March 2026.
summaries.1493: shawnalpay proposed using "period" consistently for lengths of time, replacing "term" and "duration", because #1350's contract commitments needed "term" to mean a contract provision. aws-jrmarks and robmartin33 asked to keep a Term glossary entry that points readers to Period, which shawnalpay added. ijurica suggested defining period as a time window, and SatyaVandrangi1 asked to avoid the word "condition". Members approved it and it merged in October 2025.
summaries.1500: rileyjenk requested an Invoice dataset so finance teams could reconcile FOCUS data against invoices. qquigley urged involving finance personas, and beau-nelford-anglepoint offered support. From November 2025 shawnalpay led modeling in Task Force 1 with finance experts, Matt-Cowsert gathered data generator input, and thecloudman asked for an FX rate column. #1900 advanced toward member review in February 2026, and shawnalpay closed the issue in April 2026 when #2100 merged.
summaries.1501: shawnalpay opened this pull request for #962 to add Correction Handling and Delivery Handling attributes and rework Invoice Handling. In October 2025 maintainers closed it, deferring the work until an Invoice dataset existed (#1500), but work resumed in 2026. The final version defined Replacement, Delta and Ledger correction styles and Overwrite and Append delivery, and moved Invoice Handling to an appendix. Matt-Cowsert recorded a decision not to rename the ChargeClass value "Correction", since that would be a breaking change. rileyjenk and pydi-aws warned that limits on correcting closed billing periods could deter vendors, while ijurica held that data must be accurate before being marked final; rileyjenk and ijurica converged on separating invoice status from data delivery status. Members approved it on April 2, 2026, and it was merged that month.
summaries.1513: Mostly editorial: shawnalpay bundled simple consistency fixes for the 1.3 consistency review under #1380. shawnalpay asked whether reordering requirements would change their conformance IDs, and the Maintainers confirmed in October 2025 that the IDs would stay durable. ijurica contributed edits to the dataset overview. Members approved it without objections in October 2025.
summaries.1515: shawnalpay opened this action item to define dataset and dataset artifact in the glossary, after #1464 introduced the second term, and to review every use of dataset in the specification. Matt-Cowsert suggested also covering dataset instance artifact, and ijurica proposed agreeing the glossary terms first through #1527. rileyjenk's #1568 was replaced by #1576, which Members approved on November 6, and the item was closed as completed in November 2025.
summaries.1518: ijurica's editorial PR reduced the nesting of several CommitmentDiscountQuantity requirements from three levels to two, with no material change, on the assumption that this suited conformance work better. Matt-Cowsert approved after a TF-2 review, saying it simplified the null check, and jpradocueva approved pending a check against #1209. Members approved it on 16 October 2025 and it merged.
summaries.1521: ijurica opened this editorial pull request on the Metadata specification: tidier wording, consistent use of Dataset ID and Dataset Instance ID, top-level elements reordered by dependency, and normative requirements turned from paragraphs into bullet lists, without changing intent. shawnalpay added revisions and noted inconsistent underscores in file names, proposing a separate future action item. ijurica committed bullet-list rewrites for several objects without waiting for feedback, to speed review, and asked why Recency was MAY rather than SHOULD; rileyjenk replied that Recency is not required in this version. Wrapping some examples in square brackets was left to rileyjenk or the next release, and ijurica said a metadata layout overview was planned for the next release. Members approved it without objection and it merged in October 2025.
summaries.1522: ijurica asked to align the suffixes of the date and time properties newly added to Metadata in 1.3. TF-2 agreed to standardise them, initially suggesting "last updated at", and ijurica proposed wider renaming plus naming principles for state and timestamp properties. TF-3 limited 1.3 to renaming RecencyLastUpdateDate to RecencyLastUpdated, moving the rest to #1060 and #1533. It closed as completed in October 2025.
summaries.1525: shawnalpay moved all Markdown content out of the .mdpp build files into separate overview .md files, under action item #1512, leaving the metadata folder out of scope. The change was mechanical: ijurica spotted a broken appendix table of contents and wrong file extensions, which shawnalpay fixed. Matt-Cowsert approved, noting it separated build instructions from content. Members approved it on October 16 and it merged in October 2025.
summaries.1534: rileyjenk renamed the recency metadata property RecencyLastUpdateDate to RecencyLastUpdated under action item #1522. ijurica shared naming conventions being drafted in #1533, including past-participle suffixes for state indicators and an At suffix for timestamps. shawnalpay requested fixes to a file name, the requirement wording and a broken example link, then approved. Members approved it on October 30 and it merged in October 2025.
summaries.1536: Mostly mechanical: davidearney updated the Requirements headers in column files from allocatedresourceid.md to chargeperiodend.md for #1508. shawnalpay requested changes because a trailing colon broke the PDF build and the introductory requirements sentence had to stay, following example PR #1509. davidearney fixed both, and Members approved it without objection on October 30, 2025, when it merged.
summaries.1550: shawnalpay noted in October 2025 that Section 1.8 wrongly said no conformance validators existed. mike-finopsorg offered three options: remove the section, link only the foundation's validator, or list other tools too. Matt-Cowsert preferred linking the validator without implying an exhaustive list. mike-finopsorg drafted text saying third-party tools may exist and none is mandated; it went into #1513, which members approved in October 2025.
summaries.1557: This editorial PR by davidearney standardised the Requirements headers for the columns from ChargePeriodStart through Tags. shawnalpay requested changes so that each column also kept a lead-in sentence saying it adheres to the requirements that follow, as agreed in #1536. Members approved it without objections on 30 October 2025, and it was merged that day.
summaries.1559: Editorial: for #1508, davidearney changed the Requirements headers of the contract commitment columns to match the rest of the spec. shawnalpay requested changes, asking that every column keep a lead-in sentence saying it adheres to the following requirements, following a pattern agreed in #1536. jpradocueva approved, and members approved it without objections in October 2025.
summaries.1566: ijurica applied the new dataset-level normative requirement guidelines to the Cost and Usage and Contract Commitment datasets. shawnalpay asked why DiscountHandling had moved and suggested alphabetical order, but accepted ijurica's explanation that the order put technical requirements before business ones, per the forthcoming #1529. Members approved it without objections on 30 October 2025, and it was merged.
summaries.1567: rileyjenk opened this PR to apply four entity terms consistently, service provider, host provider, data generator and invoice issuer, in place of loose uses of provider and publisher. rileyjenk renamed the new split cost allocation feature as service-provider-calculated, but the group voted for data generator, and shawnalpay committed those renames per an October 2025 TF-2 agreement. shawnalpay requested changes while agreeing with about 80% of the edits, and resolved heavy merge conflicts. ijurica supplied line-specific fixes and flagged broken titles and anchors left by the renaming. Approval was postponed to no later than 6 November 2025, when members approved it without objections, and it merged.
summaries.1568: rileyjenk proposed glossary and schema metadata fixes for the term dataset instance artifact under action item #1515. ijurica questioned the statement that a dataset instance and its artifact are the same when data is delivered through a database, and suggested editorial changes. Because the underlying files had since changed, shawnalpay recommended starting again from working_draft. rileyjenk opened #1576 instead, and this pull request was closed without merging in November 2025.
summaries.1570: Matt-Cowsert's PR, for #1458, added explicit "Cost and Usage" dataset references across column definitions and an appendix example. shawnalpay requested changes, agreeing with the appendix edits but objecting to naming the dataset in attributes, since the 1.3 team had agreed that link belongs in dataset requirements. Matt-Cowsert removed those references, shawnalpay approved, and Members approved it on October 30, 2025, when it was merged.
summaries.1582: shawnalpay opened this action item in November 2025 to fix anchor links for columns sharing a name across datasets and to document how anchors work, per #1569. ijurica noted that the PDF outline showed more heading levels than the on-page contents. mike-finopsorg opened #1656 for the link fix and asked for a separate feature request about the contents. No comment records the outcome; GitHub shows it closed as completed.
summaries.1625: shawnalpay asked that ListUnitPrice and ListCost requirements say which pricing tier they reflect, because AWS fills them from the highest tier, inflating savings. cnharris10 asked about negotiated tiers, which udam-stitcher said affect only contracted prices. udam-stitcher also noted a contradiction in the issue text and argued list price should follow the row's SKU Price ID, so existing rules may already cover tiers. It remained open, last discussed in November 2025.
summaries.1645: qquigley's PR, under #1380, fixed a copy-and-paste error and clarified the split cost example. shawnalpay relayed mike-finopsorg's suggestion to state that the ContractApplied and AllocatedMethodDetails examples describe a single Cost and Usage row, so readers do not assume AllocatedRatio sums to 1. Members approved it on December 4, 2025, and jpradocueva noted the change also went to the candidate_recommendation branch, citing #1649.
summaries.1647: jpradocueva opened this pull request for #1646 to replace every RECOMMENDED normative statement with SHOULD. shawnalpay and ijurica asked for the editorial and normative requirements guidelines to be updated too, and maintainers set it to draft on December 1, 2025 until the guidelines stopped distinguishing SHOULD from RECOMMENDED. ijurica listed further places to change in the introduction and requirements model guidelines, and kk09v suggested rewordings in several column files. On December 15 maintainers also agreed to strike OPTIONAL from the allowed keywords. Matt-Cowsert confirmed that timwright2000 for Google and vikramdesai01 for Microsoft were content with the change. Members approved it without objection on December 18, 2025, and it was merged that month.
summaries.1656: Pull request #1656, by mike-finopsorg, was mechanical work fixing HTML and PDF anchor links for columns used in more than one dataset (#1582). ijurica asked for Metadata section links to be fixed too and listed broken ones, which mike-finopsorg corrected over several passes. Matt-Cowsert requested two link fixes in the provider name files, which shawnalpay committed. Members approved it on 8 January 2026 and it merged.
summaries.1661: An editorial PR in which narlaadbe fixed minor typos for #1541. shawnalpay and jpradocueva approved it, and Members approved it without objections on December 11, 2025, when it merged.
summaries.1676: shawnalpay asked for the applicability criteria that decide when conditional columns must be present to be defined in the spec itself, not only in the downstream Requirements Model. mike-finopsorg asked whether criteria should be defined first and cited in normative text, or derived from it. shawnalpay's #2351 was merged in May 2026; the issue was reopened to add conditions to column constraint tables via #2423, and closed in July 2026.
summaries.1678: ijurica opened this PR, the first milestone of #982, to rewrite the definitions of Billed Cost and Effective Cost and remove their outdated glossary entries. robmartin33 objected to framing them as cash-based and accrual-based accounting, Matt-Cowsert wanted a section on two practitioner challenges cut, and a TF-3 meeting on 9 January 2026 agreed the wording. ljadvey warned that dropping amortization from the definition would leave practitioners asking where net amortized costs are; shawnalpay suggested citing amortization as an example. udam-stitcher kept deliberately exhaustive wording and chose "recognized" over "consumed", which has a specific FOCUS meaning. shawnalpay approved on condition that Matt-Cowsert bring back the cut amortization sentence as a normative requirement in TF-3 work. Members approved it on 29 January 2026 and it merged.
summaries.1785: This was shawnalpay's action item to draft the Invoice Detail and Billing Period datasets. shawnalpay opened #1900 in January 2026 but kept the item open to finish TODO sections, after delays from Contract Commitment work. After reviews in TF-1 brought no outstanding feedback, shawnalpay closed it as complete in February 2026.
summaries.1793: Matt-Cowsert logged this action item in December 2025 to draft a PR for #958's commitment eligibility indicator, which Task Force 3 had agreed should be a JSON structure holding the provider's term and a FOCUS category such as spend-based or usage-based. It waited on input from cnharris10, then SanjnaSrivatsaVMware published the draft PR. It was closed in January 2026, with supported-feature content still to come.
summaries.1797: mike-finopsorg reported that the FOCUS 1.3 List Unit Price requirements included a rule that really applied to ListCost and was already stated there. shawnalpay objected to parking it under the 1.4 consistency review and said it was not errata either. The March 16, 2026 Maintainers call brought it into scope, with Matt-Cowsert writing a PR. It was implemented through #2067 in March 2026.
summaries.1800: flanakin's pull request (#1094) added a Dataset Completeness attribute, first called Scenario Completeness, requiring FOCUS datasets to include x_ custom columns for native columns that FOCUS does not cover. Matt-Cowsert pushed for entity-focused wording, shawnalpay objected to any aggregation or granularity requirements, and the requirements-model JSON was dropped at mike-finopsorg's request. pydi-aws asked for SHOULD instead of MUST, warning AWS exports would exceed 100 columns; mike-finopsorg called the omission clause an impossible bar, and shawnalpay proposed relying on column selection with a default column set. sarahcloudpm raised data-volume concerns. TF2 settled on including everything and documenting exclusions with justification. shawnalpay objected that flanakin's AI-assisted workflow recommitted suggestions separately, denying commenters co-authorship. Members approved it on March 26, 2026, and it merged that month.
summaries.1803: shawnalpay logged this action item in January 2026 to draft a PR extending the Contract Commitment dataset. The work became #1924, which left draft in early February 2026 after incorporating feedback. shawnalpay closed the item on February 11, 2026, once #1924 was stable, aiming for Member review by February 17.
summaries.1816: For #1091 and FOCUS 1.4, flanakin proposed a Dataset Configuration attribute requiring that a dataset can be limited to user-selected columns while still meeting column rules. Row aggregation, time granularity, version selection and row filtering went into supporting content as deferred ideas. Matt-Cowsert wanted that deferred material out of the PR; ijurica asked how conformance works when excluded columns are referenced by others, and flanakin softened the metadata rule to SHOULD after ijurica's feedback. mike-finopsorg had requirements-model files removed until 1.3 modelling finished, and jpradocueva said the rules described the dataset rather than an attribute. shawnalpay supplied rewrites and had it applied to Contract Commitment too. flanakin also reclassified unit price columns as dimensions and posted AI-generated update summaries. Members approved it in February 2026 and it was merged.
summaries.1865: For #1844, mike-finopsorg moved column presence requirements out of individual column files and into each dataset's definition. shawnalpay noted readers would lose the presence rule beside each column's feature level and suggested a Content Constraints entry naming and linking the dataset, which mike-finopsorg added to every column. ijurica proposed matching changes to the requirements guidelines and a rule order. Members approved it without objections in February 2026.
summaries.1868: shawnalpay opened this action item to apply the file and folder naming conventions ijurica was stewarding, planned for the 1.4 consistency review. In April 2026 the Maintainers postponed it to early 1.5 to avoid merge conflicts, and in May shawnalpay handed it to flanakin. The due date was later pushed out, samantha-weymouth asked flanakin for a status update in July 2026, and the issue remains open.
summaries.1877: ljadvey's pull request for FR #1488 replaced the commitment discount appendix with 14 provider-specific scenarios for AWS, Azure and GCP, each with CSV data and column-by-column explanations. shawnalpay required a working PDF build and an overview page, and briefly insisted the PR fix SQL wrapping in the PDF before finding that problem already existed in 1.3 and opening #1965. Matt-Cowsert's large review centred on ContractedUnitPrice, which ijurica had said must equal ListUnitPrice in non-negotiated scenarios, and udam-stitcher called some cost explanations incorrect. mike-finopsorg asked for another proofreading pass, noting AI-generated content still needs the author's quality check. TF-2 then cut non-EC2 rows and savings calculations to keep the examples simple. With six approvals, Members approved it and it merged in March 2026.
summaries.1878: shawnalpay opened this placeholder in January 2026 to collect work for the FOCUS 1.4 consistency review, scheduled for April 9 to 30, and triaged each reported inconsistency into an action item or pull request. shawnalpay's own items included a dedicated Allowed Values subsection (#2106), an invoice issuer glossary entry (#2107), an explicit JSON type requirement for Tags (#2114) and dataset ordering (#2120). ijurica flagged broken links, over-linking against the editorial guidelines and inconsistent references to participating entities. davidearney logged many editorial fixes, such as header capitalization, contractions, dash style and quoting of allowed values, and agreed to bundle them into one PR, #2200, with later fixes in #2203, #2204, #2205 and #2207. shawnalpay closed the task as complete in May 2026.
summaries.1880: jpradocueva opened this action item to automate extracting normative requirements from the spec's Markdown into JSON with at least 90% accuracy. jpradocueva found that lead-in statements such as "adheres to the following requirements" carried mandatory intent without BCP-14 keywords, and proposed explicit MUST wording; mike-finopsorg preferred "MUST adhere to the following requirements". After due-date delays, tracking moved in March 2026 to #2083, with the changes in #2090.
summaries.1882: Pull request #1882, by SanjnaSrivatsaVMware, added a Commitment Program Eligibility Details column listing the commitment programs a usage row is eligible for, to support coverage calculations (#1793, FR #958). The name kept changing: flanakin asked for a Details suffix like other JSON columns, rileyjenk said the scope was too narrow, TF-3 dropped 'Discount' to cover capacity reservations and SaaS commitments, and ijurica later suggested a full rename. Matt-Cowsert twice requested changes over type contradictions and redundant requirements; negotiated programs became optional and presence rules moved to dataset level. sarahcloudpm questioned the value of listing multiple programs. At shawnalpay's suggestion, separate lists became one CommitmentPrograms array, and shawnalpay warned it would be cut from 1.4 if unresolved by 9 April. Members approved it on 9 April 2026.
summaries.1888: shawnalpay proposed in January 2026 removing ProviderName and PublisherName, deprecated in 1.3, from the 1.4 specification, and documenting how removals are done. qquigley and TechinMama took on the work with help from davidearney, and the group agreed to generalise the removal process to all spec entities, not just columns. PR #1955 was approved and merged, and shawnalpay closed it as complete in March 2026.
summaries.1897: Matt-Cowsert opened this action item to draft appendix guidance on SaaS licensing where usage cannot be tracked, such as seat-based, flat-rate and tiered pricing with committed minimums, including when EffectiveCost should equal BilledCost; it was outside the scope of #1488. Matt-Cowsert later suggested merging it with another scenario-drafting item and closed it as completed in February 2026, leaving the remaining work to task force 3.
summaries.1900: Pull request #1900, by shawnalpay, added two datasets, Invoice Detail for invoice reconciliation and Billing Period for billing cycle status, to support correction handling. rileyjenk asked about marketplace cases where both provider and invoice issuer produce invoice-like records. thecloudman argued an exchange rate column was vital; shawnalpay replied that TF-1 had not supported it, since a single invoice rate would create rounding errors against daily rates, and an effective rate can be derived. Matt-Cowsert suggested more invoice status values, but payment-related states had been ruled out of scope. ijurica wanted invoice-handling requirements from #1501 placed in these columns, and shawnalpay applied agreed changes such as making InvoiceId mandatory in Cost and Usage. Members approved it on 12 March 2026 and it merged.
summaries.1904: kk09v proposed a TagDetails JSON column for FR #1124, recording tag provenance, inherited ancestor tags and untagged but taggable sources to support tag-coverage analysis. TF2 sessions in March 2026 refined nullability and added a tag scheme glossary entry, leaving tag source conditionality as the main blocker. Maintainers agreed kk09v would refactor it to the JSON format from #2007. thecloudman asked whether the column could omit tag key-value pairs to avoid duplicating Tags and AllocatedTags; shawnalpay and kk09v argued the duplication was needed for provenance and eligibility. aws-jrmarks backed SHOULD presence on dataset-size grounds, while shawnalpay objected to a Recommended column without solid reason. Matt-Cowsert requested changes over ambiguities. In March 2026 it was descoped from 1.4, as maintainers judged it would not survive member review, and closed.
summaries.1908: flanakin proposed reclassifying four unit price columns from Metric to Dimension because summing unit prices produces meaningless values, splitting the change out of #1816. shawnalpay noted it was outside 1.4 scope and that aggregation includes averages, min and max; udam-stitcher and aws-jrmarks argued unit prices are non-additive metrics used in calculations. Maintainers agreed to keep them as metrics, and shawnalpay closed it without merging in February 2026.
summaries.1914: Matt-Cowsert opened this action item to split a reclassification of four unit price columns from metrics to dimensions out of #1816 into a separate draft pull request. flanakin created #1908, but shawnalpay considered the change outside 1.4 scope and udam-stitcher argued unit prices are metrics. TF-2 agreed the pull request had been premature, and the item was closed as completed in February 2026 as work not planned for 1.4.
summaries.1924: shawnalpay opened this PR to extend the Contract Commitment dataset with 17 columns covering commitment model, fulfilment and payment intervals, payment terms, discount and upfront percentages, lifecycle status, categories, currency and provider names, plus a JSON applicability column with its own schema and appendix scenarios. Review renamed several columns: Scope became Eligibility, then Applicability, after robmartin33 flagged overlap with FinOps Scopes, Interval became Fulfillment Interval, and Duration became Duration Type after rileyjenk's concern. ljadvey proposed dropping "Commitment" from the dataset name, which shawnalpay ruled out of scope because 1.3 had approved it. mike-finopsorg and Matt-Cowsert refined wording and constraints, and ijurica's late feedback removed Monetary Pool as a benefit category. Members approved it without objections on 12 March 2026, and it was merged.
summaries.1941: Matt-Cowsert asked for worked examples showing practitioners how AI token and image-generation billing maps onto existing FOCUS columns. TF-2 held the work until #2018 settled, then limited it to the Cost and Usage dataset and already-defined columns; ljadvey and finops-DaveMoreau built the examples in #2605, including a prepayment drawdown case.
